payload.title: Name Change After Marriage Step by Step in Australia
payload.excerpt: A name change after marriage in Australia is a choice, and it does not happen on its own: you update each record yourself.
key_takeaways: If you married in Australia, NSW, Victoria and Queensland let you take your spouse's surname using your official marriage certificate, with no formal change of name.
Agencies want the official certificate issued by the registry, not the ceremonial one signed on the day.
Following the NSW order, get the official certificate first, then update your driver licence and Medicare, which gives you the proof to change your name almost everywhere else.
If you married overseas, NSW and Victoria require an official change of name, and the Passport Office needs any document not in English translated in full.

faq.q: Do I change my name before or after the wedding?
faq.a: After. You need the official marriage certificate from the registry to change your name, and your celebrant can apply for it on your behalf.

faq.q: How long does a name change after marriage take?
faq.a: It depends on your certificate and how many organisations you tell, so ask the registry for current timing when you order. In NSW, once approved, a new driver licence arrives within 1 to 2 weeks.

faq.q: How much does it cost to change your name after marriage?
faq.a: If you married in Australia, NSW says you don't need to pay the fee for an official change of name. Your celebrant can order the official marriage certificate for you, generally at a cost. A formal change of name, which an overseas marriage needs in NSW, carries a registry fee.

faq.q: Can I travel on my honeymoon with my old passport?
faq.a: The Passport Office says that after a marriage-related change of family name you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one, and recommends booking travel in the name that's in your passport. Check the name on your tickets matches the passport you will carry.

faq.q: Can I use an overseas marriage certificate to change my name?
faq.a: Usually not on its own. NSW says an overseas marriage certificate cannot be used to change your surname, and Victoria says you need to apply to change your name.

faq.q: Can I just revert back to my maiden name?
faq.a: Yes. In Victoria, if you married in Australia and took your spouse's name, you can go back without applying to BDM, using your marriage and birth certificates and, if relevant, your divorce certificate. If you changed your name formally, NSW says you may need to apply to the registry for another legal change of name, and Victoria says you need to change your name with BDM to go back after an overseas marriage.
